Moreover, the SIW technology permits to adopt a number of antenna topologies featuring several advantages in terms of reconfigurability and dynamic performance, which becomes extremely beneficial in the synthesis of modern phased array configurations.

articleTitle: Design of a Magnetoelectric Dipole Antenna for Wideband Wide-Scanning Phased Array
abstract: A magnetoelectric dipole (MED) antenna using substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) technology has been proposed for wideband phased array application. The proposed antenna is composed of a pair of arc-shaped patches as an electric dipole and a group of circular vertical shorted vias that are equivalent to a magnetic dipole. A Γ-shaped probe feed is employed to excite the MED antenna, and some planar metal reflectors with shorted via holes are located at the corner of the antenna to improve matching of the antenna. The simulated operating band is 2.75-5.94 GHz (relative bandwidth is 73.4%) for |S11|<;-10 dB. Besides, a unit cell in an infinite array environment is simulated, which achieves more than 40.1% bandwidth with VSWR≤2.5 when scanning to -75°both in the Eand H-planes.

articleTitle: Design of a 110 GHz broadband frequency tripler using planar varistor Schottky diodes
abstract: This paper presents the design and demonstration of a 110GHz broadband varistor tripler utilizing two commercial gallium arsenide Schottky diodes from United Monolithic Semiconductor (UMS) Inc. Anti-parallel configuration eliminates even harmonics and thus no additional output filtering is needed. An accurate threedimensional electromagnetic (3D-EM) model is established to characterize the high-frequency parasitic effect of diodes. Linear and nonlinear simulations are performed iteratively to design the embedding circuit for high efficiency conversion. The whole circuit of the tripler is fabricated on RT/Rogers 5880 substrate with thickness of 0.127mm, housed in split waveguide blocks. The measured results show that with 20~22dBm input power at Ka-band, the tripler reaches maximum 9 dBm output power at 106 GHz and achieves 2.3%~5.5% efficiency across 90~120 GHz frequency band.

articleTitle: Free-Space Permittivity Measurement for Inhomogeneous PSV-Coated Si-wafer at Frequencies from 75 GHz to 325 GHz
abstract: A method to extract dielectric property of inhomogeneous PSV (Passivation)-coated Si-wafer is presented at broadband frequencies from 75 GHz to 325 GHz. Free-space measurement using continuous wave (CW) system is carried out. Numerical iterative algorithm is employed to extract permittivity from complex scattering parameters. Due to scarcity of related previous studies beyond 100 GHz, the discussions on parameters that may affect the results are also described in detail. The calculated permittivity based on the proposed method highly correlates with the analytical values.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Pattern Reconfigurable HMSIW Leaky Wave Antenna Based on Liquid Crystal Tuning Technology in Millimeter Wave Band
abstract: A pattern reconfigurable leaky-wave antenna loaded liquid crystal material (LC) is presented based on novel half mode substrate integrated waveguide (HMSIW) circuit in this paper. By loading interdigital capacitor gap (IDC), the leaky wave radiation is realized. LC-based substrate integrated waveguide can achieve bias tuning by rectangular DC ground which inside the waveguide. With liquid crystal tuning, the main beam of antenna pattern is deflected 16.In addition, in the tuning process, the gain fluctuation of the antenna is less than 1.2dB and the maximum peak gain is 10.14dBi. The proposed antenna working at millimeter-wave band and the in-band reflection coefficient is less than -10dB.

articleTitle: Transparent Broadband Wide-angle Polarization-insensitive Metasurface Absorber for Microwave Antireflection
abstract: A novel multi-layer metasurface absorber (MA) unit, which is optically transparent, broadband, wide-angle and polarization-insensitive, is designed and optimized for microwave antireflection based on the indium tin oxide (ITO) film. Theoretical simulation results show that the proposed unit exhibits a high absorption response more than 90% from 5.4 GHz to 36.7 GHz and the relative absorption bandwidth is about 148.7%. In addition, the metasurface absorber unit keeps good polarization insensitiveness and wide-incident-angle stability characteristics with the absorption property. In the meanwhile, using the indium tin oxide and the transparent polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA), the optical transparence of the patterns and substrates makes the reported metasurface absorber a promising candidate for future applications like photovoltaic solar cells and electromagnetic shielding glasses and so on. The optically transparent, broadband, wide-angle and polarization-insensitive multifunctional metasurface absorber will enable the promising application of communication-compatible multispectral stealth technology.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Bandpass Filter with Large Frequency Ratio and Independently Tunable Center Frequencies
abstract: For the first time, a dual-band bandpass filter with independently tunable center frequencies was implemented to support microwave and millimeter-wave frequency bands simultaneously. To achieve the desired high-frequency ratio, the microstrip element is combined with the metallic cavity element through the aperture coupling mechanism. Meanwhile, the proposed approach allows the independent control of the two operating frequencies. For demonstration, a tunable dual-band bandpass filter was designed, fabricated and measured. A maximum tunable frequency ratio up to 24 can be achieved together with the independent center frequency tunability.

articleTitle: L-Band 1000W Single-Chip Internally Matched GaN Amplifier
abstract: In this paper, A L-Band single-chip internallymatched AlGaN/GaN amplifier has been developed. The gate-periphery of the GaN HEMT is 55mm. The input and output matching circuit with the GaN chip are integrated in a 17.4mm×24mm ceramic package. The internally matched amplifier has demonstrated the pulse output power of over 1000W, power density of 18W/mm and the power gain of 18dB across the 1.25GHz to 1.35GHz with the voltage of 80V, and the max power added efficiency is 71.4% under the pulse condition at a duty of 1% with a pulse width of 5μs. This is the highest combination of output power, power gain and PAE from a single-chip AlGaN/GaN HEMT at L band.

articleTitle: A Novel Strip-Line Hybrid Triple-Mode SIW Filter
abstract: In this paper, a triple-mode SIW resonator based on the SIW rectangular cavity and strip-line hybrid structure are proposed. The proposed triple-mode SIW cavity excites three frequency-tunable resonant modes. A filter based on the proposed triple-mode resonator is simulated and fabricated. The filter has high out-of-band rejection and sharp skirt selectivity due to two close band transmission zeros. In addition, the operating bandwidth of this filter can be controlled by changing the length of the trip-line and the position of the perturbed metallic vias. Finally, the simulated and measured results are presented and compared to verify the design method.

articleTitle: Chipless RFID Sensor Tag for Angular Velocity and Displacement Measurement
abstract: A novel chipless RFID sensor tag is investigated for angular velocity and displacement measurement. The designed sensor tag consists of horizontal and vertical I-shaped bar resonators which are both symmetrically arranged. The whole of the longest resonators acts as a sensing element while the others are used as encoders. The angular variation can be detected by measuring the Radar Cross-Section (RCS) magnitude of the sensing element as the object, to which the tag is attached, rotates. Meanwhile, a depolarizing technique is applied, which makes the detection process more robust. In addition, due to the fact that the dual polarization (DP) can increase the encoding capacity doubly in the same frequency band, the proposed tag with a compact dimension of 22 × 30 × 0.8 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> can encode 18-bit data. As compared with angular displacement and velocity sensors based on inductive coupling modulation, the proposed sensor tag can make a significant increase of the sensing distance.

articleTitle: Switched Magnetic Field for Hybrid Wireless Positioning and Wireless Charging Using Helmholtz Coils
abstract: A gradient Helmholtz Coils model is proposed to achieve hybrid wireless positioning and wireless charging. By switching the driving source between the identical mode and the gradient mode, an alternative uniform and gradient magnetic field can be generated within the effective region. The mathematical model of the proposed coils structure is derived to achieve the optimal coil configuration. Simulation results of the detected field from the 3D probe coil is provided to demonstrate the feasibility of the wireless positioning. This model provides a simple system structure for biomedical devices which require simultaneous wireless positioning and wireless charging.

articleTitle: Design of 3-dB Differentially-Fed Tandem Directional Couplers
abstract: In this paper, for the first time the design of a tandem directional coupler operating in differential mode has been shown. To equalize phase velocities, the proposed directional coupler has been realized in homogeneous multilayer structure. To verify applicability of such a concept the 3-dB differentially-fed tandem directional coupler, operating at 1 GHz center frequency has been designed, fabricated, and measured.

articleTitle: Multi-Functional Reconfigurable Dielectric Resonant Antenna
abstract: In this paper, a novel multi-functional reconfigurable dielectric resonant antenna is proposed. It consists of a cylindrical and a sectored resonator structures, realizing the reconfigurable on polarization and radiation pattern simultaneously. Improved hybrid orthogonal network is used for feeding to provide a stable phase difference over 5 to 6 GHz band. The simulation results show that the linear polarization has an input reflection coefficient bandwidth of 22.8%, the circularly polarized has an input reflection coefficient bandwidth of 18.1%, and a 3-dB AR bandwidths of 6%. Benefited from the combination of dielectric resonant antenna with the reconfigurable structure, the design has high degree of design freedom and easy to be miniaturized.

articleTitle: A Novel Terahertz Waveguide Filter Based on MEMS Technology
abstract: This paper presents high performance 0.34THz waveguide filters based on MEMS technology. The relationship between fabrication error and filter performance was studied and a quantitative model is given. The fabrication geometrical tolerance can be controlled to be lower than 5% for iris structures (and ±5μm for resonant cavities). Our test results show a good agreement with simulation results when fabrication error is less than ~5 μm, the test result shows a performance of ~0.5dB insertion with ~5.29% relative bandwidth.

articleTitle: Improved microwave cavity sensor for sheet resistance evaluation of conductive nano-films
abstract: This work presents an improved sheet resistance evaluation sensor for conductive nano-films. The proposed sensor is based on a microwave cylindrical cavity with an aperture on one of its endplates. Conductive nano-film is placed close to the aperture and thus perturbs the electromagnetic field inside the cavity. Measurement results show that the quality factor of the cavity can be related to the sheet resistance of nano-film. The advantage of the proposed sensor is that it is able to evaluate smaller samples. Namely, it has higher spatial resolution compared with conventional cavity sensor.

articleTitle: Multi-node activity recognition based on wireless sensor network in classroom
abstract: This work constructs and discusses a multi-node wireless activity recognition system for teaching environments. The system can collect behavior data simultaneously from multiple users overall wearing the wireless sensor. Behavior data is collected and calculated from users to extract features. The features are then used to do the effective classifier training and recognize different activities. As introduced in classroom teaching, this system can provide high recognition accuracy of the student's activity and give teachers helpful information to better adjust their course. It is 94.092% in recognition accuracy as being used to recognize five daily activities of learners in classroom education.

articleTitle: Design of an Enhancement System for Personal Satellite Communication
abstract: Personal satellite communication (PSC) has applications ranging from sensitive information transmission to emergency communication in the cell network unavailable area. It is of particular interest because it has features such as high reliability, high mobility and independent from ground infrastructure. However, existing personal satellite communication technologies suffer from some inherent limitation in that the working hours of the personal terminal are not long enough and the communication could be affected by weather. Here, we propose a personal satellite enhancement system to transceive the data between installed on the solar energy unmanned aerial vehicle, could provide multi-users' access and high data rate personal communication data link. We analyze the frequency planning, access control, bandwidth effectiveness and transmission delay of the enhancement system. The proposed system could reduce the complexity of personal terminal and the adverse effect of weather condition effectively. We anticipate that the proposed system could provide new ideas on improving the PSC user experience.

articleTitle: High Aperture Efficiency Wideband TA With Low Cross Polarization
abstract: In this paper, a wideband high aperture efficiency transmitarray antenna (TA) with low cross polarization is proposed. The proposed TA unit cell is a triple-layer patches separated by 0.21-wavelength air gap, and this unit cell can achieve about 360° transmission phase range within -3dB transmission loss. The measured aperture efficiency, gain and -1dB gain bandwidth of the TA operating at 16 GHz are 64%, 26.9dBi and 14% from 15.2GHz to 17.5GHz, respectively. The proposed design has the advantages of the highest aperture efficiency, and lowest cross-polarization below -45dB compared with recently published related works. The developed unit cell has symmetric configuration, so it can also be applied to the design of dual-polarized TA design. The TA array has low fabrication difficulty and cost, and is suitable for high-gain and low cross-polarization application.

articleTitle: High-Efficiency Brewster Lens for Arbitrary Wavefront Control
abstract: A highly efficient lens is designed based on the concept of Brewster effect with near-unity transmittance at its operational band. This lens is synthesized with the effective medium approach by spatially varying material properties of its constituent unit cells. The relationship between effective permittivity and permeability of unit cells is constrained by the Brewster angle condition and transmissive phase for a given polarization and angle of incidence. It is found that zero reflection and proper phase compensation can be independently obtained for each unit cells with varying angle of incidence. The proposed design concept is verified through a demonstration of a planar lens transforming a cylindrical wave to a quasi-plane one with 96.9% efficiency.

articleTitle: Influence of Source Inhomogeneity on Compressed Sensing-based THz Imaging
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the effect of source inhomogeneity on THz imaging. The numerical analysis are conducted through obtaining the compressed data from a compressive sensing (CS) based THz imaging system in the optical-design software Zemax. The analysis results demonstrate that Peak Signal to Noise Ratio (PSNR) of the system is dramatically destroyed by inhomogeneous distribution of THz source. The combination of the real light distribution in the optimized reconstruction procedure is then proposed and its efficiency is demonstrated by simulation results. It is expected that the results in this paper may provide guidance for the high quality CS-based THz imaging in real-world application.

articleTitle: Low Speed Digital RoF Transmitter Linearizer Using Sub-band Signal Processing Technique
abstract: In this paper, we propose a digital sub-band (SB) filtering layout for Radio-over-Fiber (RoF) downlink transmitter. A proof-of-principle demonstration of 4 and 8 SB processing for a 256 QAM 100 MHz-bandwidth long-term evolution advanced (LTE-A) signal is presented. To alleviate the high processing speed required for next generation 5G signals, perfect reconstruction quadrature mirror filters (QMFs) are used to split and downsample a contiguous-carrier signal into smaller SBs: each containing part of the frequency content. Through measurements and simulation results, this paper demonstrated that the overall signal quality is maintained while achieving a reduction in the processing speed as well as an improvement in the adjacent carrier power ratio (ACPR). Our results demonstrate the advantages of the proposed technique in RoF transmitters networks.

articleTitle: Multi-Band Filters Based on Coupled-Multi-Line Cells
abstract: A class of multi-band bandpass filters (BPFs) based on the in-series cascade connection of coupled-multi-line cells is reported. This cell allows to generate multi-band responses with transmission zeros at both sides of all passbands without cross coupling between resonating nodes. Analytical formulas for the poles and transmission zeros of its associated normalized coupling routing diagram for one-to-four-passband realizations are given. Furthermore, for experimental-validation purposes, a 1.75/1.9-GHz third-order dual-band BPF prototype is manufactured in microstrip technology and characterized.

articleTitle: A 77 GHz Wideband Image Rejection Modulator with High LO-RF Isolation in 0.13 µm SiGe BiCMOS Technology
abstract: This paper presents an E-band image rejection modulator fabricated in 0.13-μm SiGe BiCMOS technology. A double-balanced Gilbert-cell based image rejection architecture is applied to provide high conversion gain and good linearity. For image signal elimination, a Lange coupler together with transformers constitutes the phase-shifting network to generate accurate quadrature-phase LO signals. For better isolation and balance, a Wilkinson power divider is employed to combine RF power. At IF frequency of 1 MHz and LO power of 0 dBm, the modulator achieves a measured conversion gain of over 6 dB from 73 GHz to 84 GHz, with a peak value of 7.9 dB at 77 GHz. The image rejection of the modulator is better than 28 dB from 66 GHz to 86 GHz and the LO-RF isolation is better than 25 dB from 67 GHz to 86 GHz. The measured output 1 dB compression point (OP1dB) is -1.9 dBm. Compared with other works, the proposed modulator achieves very wide bandwidth of image rejection and LO-RF isolation.

articleTitle: Design and Process Improvement of a Ku-band Wide Angle Low Side-lobe Frequency Scanning Antenna
abstract: In this paper, a wide-angle low-sidelobe frequency scanning antenna for radar system is designed and analyzed. The slow-wave structure is applied for beam scanning with frequency shift. The upper microstip radiation patches are excited by the coupling slots right above the slow-wave structure. The proposed antenna array has the advantage of low side lobe levels, reduced thickness, and wide scanning angle. The dimension of the antenna is 512 mm * 244 mm * 310 mm and beam scanning angle is from -28° to 33° over the frequency band of 16-17GHz. The simulated peak realized gain is 29.12 dBi, and the side-lobe is less than -25dB. The array is fabricated and measured peak realized gain is 27.7 dBi. Besides, the double-layer microstrip antenna is fabricated by using polymethacrylimide (PMI) foam material with improved performance.

articleTitle: Novel Ultra-wideband Wide-angle Scanning Phased Array
abstract: In this paper, a novel ultra-wideband phased array antenna element is designed by improving the traditional wide-angle scanning array of Planar Ultra-wideband Modular Antenna (PUMA). By using the asymmetric dipole arms and a new structure to eliminate the common-mode resonance, the bandwidth of the antenna is broadened and the scanning angle of the antenna is greatly improved. Simulation results show that the proposed antenna can scan up to ±60° in the E plane and ±45° in the H plane at a 5:1 bandwidth.

articleTitle: Maxwell’s Equations and Potentials in Dirac form using Geometric Algebra
abstract: The basis for engineering electromagnetic computations still relies on Gibbs' vector algebra. It is well known that Clifford algebra (geometric algebra) presents several enhancement on the latter. In this paper it is shown that Maxwell's equations can be cast in a form similar to Dirac equation by using spinors. Additionally, a similar relation is derived for the fields and the potentials. It is also shown that, as a consequence of using the geometric algebra approach, the Lorenz gauge comes naturally from the grade structure.

articleTitle: A Compact Dual-Polarized Patch Antenna Loaded With Metamaterial Unit Cell for Broadband Wireless Communication
abstract: A compact dual-polarized patch antenna loaded with metamaterial unit cell is presented in this paper for broadband wireless communication systems. The unit cell is composed of two crossed open loop resonators, which are printed on the crossed substrates. Thanks to the loading of the unit cell, a compact patch antenna is realized with two reflection zeroes. The antenna is driven by the differential ports to obtain high isolation and low cross-polarization. The proposed antenna was fabricated and measured for verification. Measured results show that the proposed antenna has the impedance bandwidth of 17 % for S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> <; -10 dB with the cross polarization lower than -33 dB. Both the simulated and measured results prove that the proposed antenna can be a good candidate for the wireless communication.

articleTitle: Optimization algorithm of Gaussian beam expansion Based on Point matching
abstract: In order to analyze the electrically large objects using in satellite communication or other fields, the quasi-optical techniques have been widely applied in millimeter and submillimeter wave band. Gaussian beam expansion (GBE) and Point matching (PM) are two methods to expand the electromagnetic field into the Gaussian beams (GBs). And combining the advantages of two methods, we propose an optimization algorithm (OA) balanced the accuracy and time-consuming. Details of three methods are discussed. The OA method shows good performance among these three methods.

articleTitle: Microwave Meta-lens for Generating Polarization-Independent refracted waves
abstract: In this paper, a transmissive-type metalens is proposed to realize independent manipulation of orthogonal circularly polarized wave in microwave region. Based on the combination of propagation phase and geometry phase principles, the opposite circularly polarized transmitted wave can be deflected into independent and arbitrary directions. Experimental measurement are conducted and effectively verified the feasibility of the proposed theory for artificial manipulation of circular polari-zation manipulation in microwave region.

articleTitle: An Inductorless Power-Optimized Dual-Mode LNTA in a GNSS Receiver for Portable Devices
abstract: There is a great increasing demand to embed GNSS receivers on portable devices, because they can provide much higher positioning accuracy and better availability compared with GPS-only receivers. However, portable devices have strong limitations on power consumption and area. In order to realize a low power and compact GNSS receiver, this paper presents both system level and circuit level solutions. In the system level, a two-state GNSS receiver architecture is introduced with acquisition phase and tracking phase to optimize the power consumption. In the circuit level, a dual-mode inductorless LNTA with adaptive bias and with an active inductor for gain boosting is proposed. This LNTA is designed and layout in a 40nm CMOS technology.

articleTitle: Application Oriented Identification of External Influence Factors on Sensing for Validation of Automated Driving Systems
abstract: Validation is essential for the development of automated driving systems (ADS). The complexity of these systems raises the difficulty of testcase generation for validation. Combination of conventional specification-based method and risk-based method is a possible way to systematically and efficiently achieve test cases. As a prerequisite for the risk-based testcase generation, external influence factors on the ADS capabilities should be identified. Since environment perception sensors are the main interfaces between external world and ADS systems, the external influence factors on sensing are the main factors which influence the system capabilities, and therefore should firstly be identified for the sake of testcase generation. In this paper, a method is introduced to identify external influence factors on sensing of ADS. As an example, the influence factors on adaptive cruise control (ACC) system are analyzed and identified.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Beam Transforming Lens with 3D Printing Technology
abstract: In this paper, a discrete dielectric lens is presented. The proposed lens can convert an incident Gaussian beam in millimeter wave band to a plane wave. The unit cells of the transforming lens are cuboid elements drilled with air holes on dielectric substrate. The insertion phase distribution before and after the lens is calculated through the paraxial Gaussian beam formula and the phase shift is realized by different air hole radius and different substrate thickness. The 3D printing technology is employed to fabricate the lens. The results show that the plane wave transformed through the lens has very good performance. The gain is greater than 36.1dBi at 35GHz.

articleTitle: Demonstration of Concurrent Dual-Band 1-bit Envelope Delta-Sigma Modulated LTE Radio-over-Fiber Transmission
abstract: With the growing demand for cloud radio access networks, mobile fronthaul networks must stay adaptable, efficient and cost-effective. To simplify fronthaul transmission systems, 1-bit delta-sigma modulation (DSM) radio over fiber (RoF) transmission has been considered promising, in which 1-bit DSM technique is used to simplify remote radio units. Moreover, carrier aggregation is a key technique for increasing fronthaul transmission capacity. This work demonstrates, for the first time, concurrent dual-band 1-bit envelope DSM 64-QAM 20-MHz LTE signals transmitted over RoF system. It is shown that carrier aggregation combined with 1-bit delta-sigma modulation is a possible promising technique for high-capacity fronthaul transmission.

articleTitle: Improved Incoherent Back Projection Imaging based on Self-amplitude Weighting and Multiplicative Tomography Weighting
abstract: An improved incoherent back projection (BP) imaging method is proposed, in which self-amplitude weighting is applied to improve the resolution of each coarse image and multiplicative tomography weighting is applied to suppress the background interference as well as to further enhance the final image resolution. Performance of this method is investigated through numerical simulation and experiment. The results show that, compared with traditional BP imaging method, the proposed method achieves remarkably improved resolution and background suppression. Therefore, this improved BP imaging method is a good solution to high-performance radar imaging.

articleTitle: A Joint Receiver Detection Scheme of Wireless Power Transfer System
abstract: This paper proposes an automatic device detection and access control scheme for coupled magnetic resonance wireless power transfer (WPT) system. This system uses phase shift detection and Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) feedback to jointly estimate the state of energy receiver device. The BLE transmits the device registration information to request the wireless charging service, and the detected phase shift at the transmitter can monitor the device state in real time. Based on the experimental results, system successfully detects a device within the scope of power transfer and starts power transmission. This joint scheme can effectively reduce detecting power at high frequencies with a simplified circuit.

articleTitle: Building Simple and Effective Metasurfaces by Coarse Discretization
abstract: This work summarizes the authors recent research experiences and identifies advantages which one can gain by designing a metasurface with coarse discretization. Whereas most metasurfaces approximate a continuous impedance variation with a finely-discretized one, we show that in some cases coarse-grained discretization yields surprising benefits. In the presentation, we will summarize our recent works which show that the coarse dis-cretization paradigm produces metasurface designs which are power efficient, simple to fabricate, and feature robust and broadband operation beyond traditional continuous metasurfaces. We will also preview our ongoing works in applying this paradigm to improve communication and imaging devices.

articleTitle: A Thin Wideband Absorber Using Resistive Frequency Selective Surface
abstract: A thin wideband resistively loaded absorber with frequency selective surface (FSS) is presented. A unit cell of the absorber contains a "c" shaped metallic dipole which printed on the substrate, loaded with a lumped resistor in the middle. A PEC ground plane was under the substrate. The substrate material chosen is FR4, having a dielectric constant of 4.4, a loss tangent of 0.02 and a thickness of 1mm. Simulation results show that the absorption coefficient of the proposed structure is greater than 90% from 4.07GHz to 16.54GHz with 121% operating frequency band, while the thickness is less than 8% of the free space wavelength at the lowest operation frequency. In addition, the effects of structure parameters of the unit cell and various incident angles on the absorption properties were analyzed.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Ultra-Wideband Dipole Antenna Utilizing A Concaved Arm
abstract: A miniaturized ultra-wideband planar antenna composed of a dipole and a concaved arm is proposed. By simply placing a concaved arm near the original dipole, a 45% area reduction in terms of electrical wavelength can be realized. The proposed antenna features a measured relative bandwidth of 133% from 2 GHz to 9.9 GHz and satisfactory radiation properties across the band. The design exhibits a physical size of 41.5 mm×41.5 mm, equivalent to a compact electrical size of 0.28 λ×0.28 λ at 2 GHz. A good agreement is achieved between the simulation and the measurement.

articleTitle: A Wideband Tightly Coupled Wide-angle Impedance Matching Layer
abstract: This paper proposed a wide-angle impedance matching (WAIM) layer for wideband phased array antennas. The proposed WAIM is based on the tightly coupled concept which introduces an additional capacitance between unit cells and provides a wide operating bandwidth. To study the scanning ability of the array, a 32 by infinite and an infinite by 32 linear arrays are analyzed. Viewing from the simulated results, by adding the proposed WAIM over a phased array antenna, the common bandwidth is improved to around 64.6% (from 5.37 to 10.5 GHz) with the scanning ability of ±60° in E-, H- and D-plane. Besides, the WAIM has the advantage of low profile and light weight properties.

articleTitle: Self-Packaged Ultra-Wideband Balanced Bandpass Filter Using Multilayer Liquid Crystal Polymer Circuit Technology
abstract: An ultra-wideband balanced bandpass filter (BPF) by using multilayer liquid crystal polymer (LCP) circuit technology with self-packaging feature is presented in this paper. The differential-mode (DM) half circuit of the proposed filter is provided and analyzed, showing that the balanced filter exhibits a four-pole ultra-wideband Chebyshev filtering response. In addition, the common-mode (CM) signals can be suppressed in a wide bandwidth region owing to the all-stop coupled-line topology in the CM equivalent circuit. Finally, an LCP balanced BPF with ultra-wideband Chebyshev response is designed, fabricated and measured. Simulated and measured results are recorded in good agreement, well validating the design method.

articleTitle: A Monolithically Integrated 80-GHz Full-Wave Rectenna With Silicon Schottky Diodes Under MOTT Operation
abstract: A monolithically integrated rectenna (rectifying antenna) operating at 80 GHz with a total chip area of 4 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> is implemented using SIMMWIC (Silicon-based Monolithic Microwave Integrated Circuit) technology. By applying four embedded 6 μm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> Schottky diodes under MOTT operation, a full-wave bridge rectifier circuit is efficiently integrated to a bow-tie antenna. Under RF-excitation in frequency range of 75 - 90 GHz, a receiving profile of conversion voltage around 80 GHz is clearly characterized, which is quite well consistent with the bandwidth property of the integrated bow-tie antenna. Under biasing current of 10 nA, the implemented rectenna could achieve maximal conversion voltage of 50 mV at the detecting distance of 10 cm.

articleTitle: A UAV-Mountable Flat Array Antenna System
abstract: In this paper, we suggest a method to design a small antenna system apt for the attachment to the drone with multi-propellers. Since each of multi-propellers is part of a branch connected to the center of the drone, a flat radial power divider is designed to feed antennas adhering to the propellers, instead of the Wilkinson power divider. For the frequency of 2.4 GHz to build a wireless link between the quadcopter and the ground, the 4-way radial power divider and 4 antennas are designed for the same frequency and light weight.

articleTitle: Linear-in-dB CMOS RF Amplitude Comparator with ±20 dB Range
abstract: This paper presents a CMOS RF amplitude comparator, which comprises a matched pair of demodulating logarithmic amplifiers and a combination stage. The circuit can generates a dc voltage proportional to the magnitude ratio between two input signals over a wide frequency range. The chip occupies an active area of 0.42mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> (including pads) using a 0.18-μm RF CMOS technology. Under a single 1.8V supply voltage, the total power dissipation is 40mW. Measurement results demonstrate that the amplitude comparator can provide an accurate measurement of either gain or loss over a ±20 dB dynamic range up to 500MHz, while the logarithmic accuracy is within ±1dB.

articleTitle: A New Scheme of Applying Multilevel Green’s Function Interpolation Method for the Analysis of Metasurface Antennas
abstract: This paper presents a new scheme of applying multilevel Green's function interpolation method (MLGFIM) for the analysis of the metasurface antennas. Considering the very thin thickness of metasurface structure, instead of using cube interpolation, the new scheme of MLGFIM implements cuboid interpolation to enhance the efficiency. Multilayered medium Green's function is used to reduce the number of unknowns. Moreover, a parallelized MLGFIM based on OpenMP is used to further speed up the computation. A block matrix preconditioner is applied to accelerate the iterative solver. A numerical example of a metasurface antenna is given to validate the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method.

articleTitle: High-power microwave photodiodes with Schottky contact based on InAlAs/InGaAs/InP heteroepitaxial structures
abstract: Dark current-voltage characteristics, sensitivity and microwave characteristics of photodiodes based on InAlAs/InGaAs (0.6-1.5 μm)/InP(001) heteroepitaxial layers with Schottky barrier and mesa structure were studied. It is shown that the dark current at reverse bias of 2 V for photodiodes with diameters from 10 to 40 μm does not exceed 1×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-10</sup> A. The sensitivity of photodiodes of different diameters with an InGaAs absorbing layer of 640 nm thick is not less than 0.55 A/W. For Schottky photodiodes with a diameter of 15 μm, cutoff frequency is 28 GHz and maximal output microwave power is 58 mW at the frequency of 20 GHz.

articleTitle: Bifunctional Meta devices based on frequency-dependent digital coding-Metasurface
abstract: Integration of multiple functionalities into the same meta-device is crucial and is the hot topic of research these days. In this article, we present frequency dependent bifunctional coding metasurface (MS). Sixteen distinct particles are designed which have independent distinct reflection phases in lower X-band and higher Ku-band. We aim to design different bifunctional coding MSs with proper selection of coding particles and proper spatial distribution of them. Three contributions are provided in this work. In the first stage, we present a coding MS which can focus the reflected waves in the lower band and defocus the same in a higher band. In the second case, a MS is de-signed which shape the reflected field in the quad beam in the lower band and provide an anomalous reflection in the higher band. In the last case, a MS is designed which can split the reflected field into two equal parts in lower band and provide an anomalous reflection in the higher band. The concept can be further extended to realize multiple functionalities in multiple bands and can be extended to realize similar functionalities in THz and optical regimes.

articleTitle: Multi-port Filtering Power Dividing Networks
abstract: Multi-port filtering power dividing networks have been applied widely in modern communication systems due to their high integration level by fusing filtering function and power dividing function into one component. The reported filtering power dividing networks are realized by using filters cascading to power dividing network or using the two identical filtering structures symmetrically coupled to one input feed line, which always suffer from large circuit size. In this paper, three different methods for size reduction are reviewed, summarized and compared with each other, such as utilizing filtering structures to replace the quarter-wavelength transmission structures of power dividing network, using couplings between the four resonators formed in a ring-type coupling topology, as well as employing one filtering structure coupled with input/output feed lines. Each method is demonstrated by one specific case.

articleTitle: Ultrasensitive Terahertz High-Tc Superconducting Receivers
abstract: This paper reviews our major technical achievement in high-T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> superconducting (HTS) terahertz (THz) receivers or heterodyne mixers in recent years. By virtue of innovative on-chip antenna/circuit designs, accurate device modelling and simulation, and advanced YBa2Cu3O7-x (YBCO) step-edge junction technology, we have successfully developed a series of HTS Josephson THz mixers with superior performance in terms of operating temperature, intermediate-frequency (IF) bandwidth, conversion gain and noise temperature. These mixers serve as promising receiver frontends for THz wireless communication and sensing systems.

articleTitle: A Concurrent Dual-Band Square Root-Based Model Based on Memory Polynomial for Closely Spaced Signals
abstract: In this paper, a novel polynomial model has been proposed to solve the problem of spectral overlap occurs in close dual-band. The proposed model effectively compensates for nonlinear distortion in closely spaced multi-carrier signals. The experimental results show that the proposed model can reduce more than 75% baseband sampling rate compared with the broadband digital predistortion (DPD) model. Moreover, the proposed model can achieve the similar adjacent channel power ratios (ACPRs) as with the broadband DPD model and more than 15dB ACPRs improvement compared with the two dimensional digital predistortion (2D-DPD) model.

articleTitle: A Wideband Circularly Polarized Slotted Patch Antenna
abstract: A low profile left-hand circularly polarized (LHCP) omnidirectional antenna is presented. The proposed antenna is consisted of a metasurface-inspired periodic patch and a feeding patch. By introducing several curved slots on the feeding patch, the two orthogonal polarized components with equal magnitude and a 90° phase difference are generated to realize CP omnidirectional radiation pattern. The simulated results show that the antenna not only has a wide operating impedance bandwidth of 17.3% and a 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth of 12.2%, but also achieves a low profile of 0.06λo (λo is the wavelength at lower frequency in the free space).

articleTitle: A Polarization Switchable Ultra-Wideband Horn Antenna with Feeding Network
abstract: A polarization switchable ultra-wideband horn antenna with feeding network is designed and implemented. A single antenna can realize four switchable polarization modes (vertical polarization, horizontal polarization, left-hand circular polarization, and right-hand circular polarization) with ultra-wideband characteristics in the microwave and millimeter wave frequency band by an electronically controlled mechanical switch. TTL (Transistor-Transistor Logic) level is adopted as controlled electrical signal. The antenna can significantly improve test efficiency by avoiding manual switching of the antenna polarization mode. The presented antenna has a super wide bandwidth of 9.3GHz, worked well from 0.7GHz to 10GHz. Measured results for VSWR, radiation pattern, and gain of the designed horn antenna are provided.

articleTitle: Ultra-wideband RF Transceiver Based on Radio over Fiber Technique
abstract: The architecture of an ultra-wideband, supporting remote radio transceiver and designed using radio over fiber technique is proposed. This system works in the frequency range between 6GHz to 18GHz, and the remote distance reaches more than 200m. The gain values of the uplink and the downlink are 24.7±1dB and 4.8±1.2dB, respectively. The noise figures of both links are less than 20dB, and the phase linear jitters are no more than ±20°. Each module is fabricated using hybrid optoelectronic micro-assembly technology, whose volume is less than 85×40×15mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>.

articleTitle: Pattern Reconfigurable Metasurface Antenna with Five States
abstract: This paper introduces a low profile radiation pattern reconfigurable antenna with five states using metasurface superstrate. The proposed antenna consists of a planar slot coupling antenna with an array of metallic rectangular patches with three sets of switches which can be view as a reconfigurable metasurface superstrate. There are five operating states of radiation patterns generated from the proposed antenna by controlling the working states of the switches. The radiation pattern would steer to 0°, ±30° and ±90° with respect to the normal direction in H plane. Furthermore, the overlap simulated -10 dB impedance bandwidth associated with all pattern modalities is 9.8% from 5.8 to 6.4 GHz. This reconfigurable antenna can form a C-band beam steering array with a total profile of 0.08λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> (4mm) at its centre operating frequency.

articleTitle: Implementation of a Two-Input Digitally Assisted Doherty Transmitter for Enhanced Performance
abstract: This work presents implementation of digitally assisted dual input Doherty power amplifier with enhanced performance in terms of power and efficiency. The efficiency enhancement is achieved by incorporating adaptive phase alignment mechanism. The alignment mechanism is implemented to characterize the imbalances between two inputs of Doherty power amplifier in terms of frequency dependent as well as power dependent phase. The proposed theory is validated with a 50 W Doherty power amplifier. The measured results show that the circuit gives upto 56% efficiency around 8-9 dB back-off, where, around 10% improvement is observed compared to its analog counterpart. The circuit also qualifies spectral mask when characterize with a single carrier 5 MHz modulated signal.

articleTitle: Machine learning based Pulsed IV behavioral model for GaN HEMTs
abstract: A novel Pulsed IV (PIV) behavioral model for Gallium Nitride (GaN) High Electron-Mobility Transistor (HEMT) based on machine learning technique is described in this paper. As one of the core methods of machine learning technique, Bayesian inference is used to build this new model. The performance of the proposed model is validated through experimental test examples. The model can very accurately predict the PIV curves of a 10W GaN HEMT at different pulse widths and duty cycles from isothermal up to the safe-operating area limit, with high voltage drain-source pulses, indicating that the proposed model can include both the thermal and dispersion effect in it precisely and effectively.

articleTitle: Revue on Designing Broadband Ultra-Thin Radar Absorbers based on Periodical Structures
abstract: In this paper, we propose a review on the design of broadband electromagnetic absorbers based on periodic structures. The dimensions of the periodic structures may be much smaller than the wavelength (≤ λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>/10) of the incident signal; it is metamaterial, or less than the wavelength (≈λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>/3), forming frequency selective surface (FSS). For a certain central operating frequency, the important criteria to optimize are the bandwidth, the absorption rate throughout the frequency band and the relative thickness of the substrate to the Rozanov limit thickness. The method consists in finding a number of electrical and / or magnetic resonances fairly close to each other for the periodic structure and optimizing the dimensional parameters in order to increase the absorption rate along the largest possible band. Example of different structures will be presented. For further analysis of the physics of the absorption mechanism, surface current distributions are observed at each eigen-frequency. The polarization and angle insensitivities are studied. Measurements have been carried out in an anechoic chamber in the frequency domain for different polarizations and incidence angles. The simulation results of the electromagnetic absorption are in agreement with the measurements. The experimental results are very promising and the absorbers can be used to tackle electromagnetic interferences (EMI) for a large domain of applications.

Author Keywords: ration of the real and limit thicknesses

articleTitle: A Symbiosis Approach to Predict On-Wafer Calibration Drift Error at mm-Wave Frequency
abstract: In this paper, a novel symbiosis approach is introduced to predict the on-wafer vector calibration drift error, hence the consistency of S-parameter measurement data, especially in mm-wave frequency band, will be greatly improved. This approach is based on the assumption that the calibration condition of measurement bench is symbiosis with the observable measurement parameters. The paper start with the analyzing of the drift error of a real on-wafer measurement system, then established a symbiosis drift model using support vector regression method to extract the model parameters. Experimental test examples are presented, revealing that this novel methodology provides a very efficient way to predict drift error and prolong the stability of on-wafer measurement system at mm-wave frequencies.

articleTitle: Design of a Wideband Vortex Beam Reflectarray Using Subwavelength Element
abstract: A new subwavelength reflective unit cell is designed and used in reflectarray to generate orbital angular momentum (OAM) waves. The metallic single layer subwavelength element consists of a cross dipole patch, four symmetric square patches and a loop patch, which is printed on one side of a substrate layer. An air layer is also inserted between metallic ground and the substrate. Size of the square unit cell is quarter wavelength at designed frequency and it achieves 360° reflection phase range. A reflectrarray is designed to generate OAM waves of mode 1 for linearly polarized feed at 6 GHz. Using the proposed subwavelength element, its far-field radiation patterns and E-field phase distribution are analyzed through CST Microwave Studio. The simulated results show that the required OAM waves are generated successfully with a maximum gain of 23.3 dBi at 6 GHz.

articleTitle: A Novel Angle Sampling Algorithm for 3D Spatial Channel Models
abstract: This paper discusses a novel 3-D channel sampling method, with an emphasis on ray-based spatial channel. A novel 3-D spatial angle sampling method based on improved particle swarm optimization (PSO) is proposed. Whether the spatial angle spreads of spatial clusters are large or small, the proposed method has good performance in approximating the target spatial channel with 20 plane waves (i.e. sinusoids). In the simulation section, we compare the performance of this algorithm with equal power method in detail. Simulation results show that the sampling method based on improved PSO presents good performance in matching the spatial correlation and temporal correlation with the target one.

articleTitle: A High-efficiency Dual-band Deflector Based on Geometric Metasurface in the X-Band
abstract: Dual-band metasurface with high efficiency is highly desired for the electromagnetic integrated system. In this paper, a dual-band transmissive meta-atom is proposed to work at cross-polarized mode for the circularly polarized incidence. The meta-atom could achieve a 360° phase coverage with conversion efficiencies better than 70% at two frequencies of X-band simultaneously. As a proof of concept demonstration, a dual-band deflector based on metasurface is designed to deflect the incident wave to the anomalous directions with arbitrary deflection angles. The simulated results show a good expected performance, which could pave the way towards high-efficiency integrated components.

articleTitle: Recent Progress of Waveguide Two-plane Couplers
abstract: This paper deals with the operation and the wideband design of the waveguide two-plane coupler and the 64x64-way one-body two-dimensional beam-switching Butler matrix using the couplers as key components.

articleTitle: Integration of V-band and W-band Antennas with SPDT Switch on Fan-Out Wafer Level Packaging (FOWLP)
abstract: This paper presents the integration of V-band and W-band antennas with SPDT switch on fan-out wafer level packaging (FOWLP) with a compact size of 16×10×0.35 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. A wide band chip to package transition is designed on redistribution layers (RDLs) to minimize the insertion loss between chip and antennas. Microstrip grid array antennas are designed and optimized at 60 GHz and 80 GHz. The antennas are fed by chip signal which is coupled through a slot in the ground plane. The simulation results show 10-dB impedance bandwidth of 9 GHz and 7.2 GHz for V-band and W-band, respectively, and maximal peak realized gain of 12.84 dBi and 14.42 dBi for V-band and W-band, respectively.

articleTitle: A General Method to Construct Arbitrary Passive S-parameter Network Using the Synchronously Tuned Coupling Resonators
abstract: In this paper, we discuss a general method to construct arbitrary passive reciprocal Scattering parameter (S-parameter) network, which may represent a functional device or a network composed by a series of devices, using the topology of synchronously tuned coupling resonators (STCR). To achieve this aim, firstly, we generalize the common STCR circuit from two-port case to arbitrary multi-port case. Then, with the help of matrix decomposition technology, the relationship between the S-parameter and the coupling coefficient matrix is constructed. On the basis of this formula, we further demonstrated that the arbitrary lossless reciprocal S-parameter matrix can be constructed by less than N+2 resonators, who resonance at the frequency of given frequency. In addition, cooperating with the method to extend a lossy network to a lossless network, this method will help us to achieve a general method to construct the narrow band arbitrary passive reciprocal S-parameter network using a fixed automated design procedure.

articleTitle: A LTCC Ridge SIW Bandpass Filter for Q-band applications
abstract: In this paper, a Q-band four-order bandpass filter based on ridge substrate integrated waveguide (RSIW) is presented by using low temperature co-fired ceramic (LTCC) technology. A CPW-SL-RSIW transition is designed for this filter. Prototype of both transition and filter have been fabricated. Good agreements between simulated and measured results are obtained.

articleTitle: Microwave single-photon detection based on dressed-state engineering
abstract: Single photon detection is a requisite technique in quantum-optics experiments in both the optical and the microwave domains. However, the energy of microwave quanta are four to five orders of magnitude less than their optical counterpart, making the efficient detection of single microwave photon extremely challenging. Here, we demonstrate the detection of a single microwave photon propagating through a waveguide. The detector is implemented with an "impedance-matched" artificial Λ system comprising the dressed states of a driven superconducting qubit coupled to a microwave resonator. We attain a single-photon detection efficiency of 0.66±0.06 with a reset time of ~400 ns. This detector can be exploited for various applications in quantum sensing, quantum communication and quantum information processing.

articleTitle: Packaging-in-Dielectric Liquid Patch Antenna
abstract: A liquid patch antenna fully packaging-in-dielectric is presented for the first time. The proposed liquid patch antenna mainly consists of three parts: dielectric hollow cavities, conductive liquid and an SMA connector. The dielectric hollow cavities are made by 3D printing technique in-one-go. There are two hollow cavities embedded in a T-shaped dielectric box, a rectangular cavity placed at the upper part acting as the radiating element, and a non-planar cavity with a central groove under the radiating element serving as the ground plane. The radiating element and ground plane are metallized by filling high-conductivity single-walled carbon nanotube paste. The proposed antenna is designed at 5.2 GHz. Preliminary results show that the liquid patch antenna produces a good impedance matching and acceptable radiation characteristics at the desired frequency. As a proof of concept demonstration, this work presents a novel method for designing RF devices combining 3D printing technique with conductive liquids. Furthermore, due to the fluidity of liquid conductive materials, it is easy to manipulate the antenna's radiation performances by adjusting the amount of conductive liquids.

articleTitle: A Low-Loss Balanced Dielectric Strip Resonator Filter
abstract: In this paper, a low-loss balanced bandpass filter (BPF) based on half-wavelength dielectric strip resonator is proposed, which consists of a thin dielectric strip with high permittivity and a low-permittivity substrate with bottom ground plane. The dielectric strip is used to replace the metal strip of the traditional microstrip line. Since there is no induced surface current on the dielectric strip, the unloaded quality factor (Qu) of the proposed resonator can be improved significantly, especially at high frequency. Meanwhile, the proposed resonator can be easily excited by the differential tapped microstrip lines for constructing the balanced BPF because its odd symmetric E-field distribution is similar to the microstrip counterpart. A prototype of the balanced BPF is simulated to show the advantages of the dielectric strip resonator.

articleTitle: Characterization of Two-Dimensional Surfaces Based on Generalized Boundary Conditions and Surface Susceptibilities
abstract: This paper presents a review on generalized boundary conditions (GBCs) in surface electromagnetics (SEM) for characterization of two-dimensional surfaces. Five representative features are chosen to describe electromagnetic characteristics of surfaces, according to which GBCs for different kinds of surface problems can be derived. Based on GBCs, scattering properties of given surfaces can be computed analytically, once their characteristic parameters, the effective surface susceptibilities, are determined from limited sets of full-wave simulations.

articleTitle: 60-GHz High Gain Planar Aperture Antenna Using Low-Temperature Cofired Ceramics (LTCC) Technology
abstract: This paper presents a new single-ended-fed planar aperture antenna using low-temperature co-fired ceramics (LTCC) process technology. The proposed antenna not only inherits the merits of the aperture antennas including high gain, wide bandwidth, but also exhibits advantages of low profile and compact size. The aperture is excited by a cross-shaped patch and a loop-shaped balun structure placing below the patch. In this way, the energy can propagate on the patch in a traveling wave form and illuminate the aperture with uniform E-field distributions. Therefore, the antenna achieves good electrical and radiation performances, which are comparable to its balancedfed counterparts, while processing a simplified structure. Measured results demonstrate that the impedance bandwidth of the antenna covers the 60-GHz license-free band (57-64GHz) and the maximum gain can reach 11.5 dBi with a cavity size of only about 27 mm2.

articleTitle: Tunable Terahertz Absorbers and Photodetectors based on Graphene
abstract: This work will address the recent developments of graphene-based tunable terahertz absorber and photodetector for potential applications.

articleTitle: A Review of Dynamically Tunable Attenuators Based on Graphene
abstract: As a two-dimension planar material with zero-gap structure, graphene has a lot of outstanding properties in microwave frequency band. The most noticeable characteristic of graphene at microwave frequencies is the possibility to electronically modify its surface impedance, just like a tunable resistance film. Due to this characteristic, the graphene material have been used to design tunable attenuators. In this paper, we review the development of dynamically tunable attenuators based on graphene which are all validated by experiments.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of A Real-time Baseband Adaptive Digital Interference Canceller
abstract: In this paper, a baseband digital canceller is designed and implemented to cancel the co-site interference. Especially, in order to achieve high-speed low-latency cancellation performance, a transposed form retimed delayed LMS (TFRDLMS) filter structure is introduced and extended to complex signal form. In the proposed complex TF-RDLMS filter, the basic Processing Module (PM) is established with a set of real cross-coupling signal flows. Then, the canceller is implemented with Xilinx field programmable gate array (FPGA) chip by cascading several PMs. Finally, the validity and effectiveness of the implemented canceller is confirmed by experimental results. It is shown that the canceller can achieve 31 dB and 27 dB cancellation performance for 5 MHz and 10 MHz interference signal, respectively.

articleTitle: A Self-Packaged SISL Coupler Using Patterned Ground Structure With Stopband
abstract: This paper presents a self-packaged branch-line coupler based substrate integrated suspended Line (SISL) platform. Patterned ground structure is designed to achieve good stopband property. As compared with the previous defected ground structure (DGS) which needs additional shielding or supporting structures for practical engineering, the proposed patterned ground structure is embedded inside the self-packaged SISL multi-layer structure, and no additional shielding structure is required. Fabricated by using standard printed circuit board (PCB) process, the implemented SISL branch-line coupler is in a self-packaged form. The measured stopband is up to 3 times of the center frequency of 2.79 GHz. In a bandwidth of 48%, the measured return loss and isolation are better than 14.5 dB. This paper shows a good application method of using the patterned ground structure on SISL platform.

articleTitle: A Novel Design of Dual-Band Dual-Polarized Base Station Antenna Based on Frequency Selective Surface
abstract: A novel dual-band dual-polarized antenna with frequency selective surface for base station operating over 1.3-2.2 GHz and 3.3-4.0 GHz is presented in this paper. The antenna is composed of a lower-band (LB) element, four upper-band (UB) elements, a frequency selective surface, a metal reflector and some metal baffles. A small overall size of the antenna can be obtained by placing four UB elements upon the LB element which is only 0.57λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> × 0.57λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> × 0.28λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> (λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> is the free-wavelength at 1.75 GHz). In order to reduce the mutual coupling between the LB and UB elements, a frequency selective surface is placed between the UB and LB elements. Simulated results show that the proposed antenna can get a high port isolation and stable radiation pattern over 51% impedance bandwidths in lower band and 19% impedance bandwidths in upper band.

articleTitle: A Broadband High-Efficiency Reflectarray Antenna Using Single-Layer Dipole Element Loaded With T-Shaped Stubs
abstract: A broadband high-efficiency reflectarray antenna using single-layer dipole element loaded with T-shaped stubs is proposed. The reflectarray unit cell is composed of a dipole element with two T-shaped stubs attached to each end of the dipole. A linear phase response with a coverage about 420°is obtained by the proposed element. An offset-fed reflectarray antenna comprising 441 elements is designed, fabricated, and measured. The measured gain is 25.7 dBi at the design frequency of 10 GHz, corresponding to an aperture efficiency of 66.6%. In addition, a wide 1-dB gain bandwidth of 24% is achieved.

articleTitle: The DA-pHEMT heterostructures for power microwave transistors
abstract: The structural, transport and optical properties of DA-pHEMT heterostructures are considered. Despite the high 2DEG density (~4×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup>), parallel conductance is almost lacking in DA-pHEMT heterostructures: the electron density in the parallel conducting layer does not exceed 11% of the 2DEG density, and the electron mobility is lower than the 2DEG mobility by a factor of more than 2.5. It was determined that the beryllium concentration in the undoped InGaAs QW does not exceed 2×0<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup> in spite of the Be segregation from the p<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>-doped barriers during the epitaxy growth. The results of the development of powerful DA-pHEMT are presented. Transistors with a gate length of 0.4-0.5 μm and a total gate width of 0.8 mm at a frequency of 10 GHz have a gain of more than 9 dB, an output power density of more than 1.6 W/mm, a power added efficiency up to 50%.

articleTitle: A Novel Dandelion Topology for Multiport Filtering Power Divider
abstract: This paper presents a dandelion topology for multi-port (1-to-N) filtering power divider, which can be applied to either the single-ended or balanced designs. Compared with the traditional tree topology, the number of resonators is reduced significantly. Meanwhile, the filtering order and the port number are mutually independent. Based on this topology, the two functions of filtering and power dividing can be designed independently. Three prototypes with equal/unequal split ratio are simulated to show the advantages of the proposed topology.

articleTitle: A Single-Layer Integrated Coding Metasurface with Flexible Beam Controlling
abstract: This paper presents a single-layered coding metasurface with inherently integrated feeding source. It alleviates the feeding blockage and alignment issues in conventional coding metasurface, and achieves a low-profile dimension. The working principle of the proposed coding metasurface is introduced followed by an example demonstration working at millimeter-wave band. It is applied with a chessboard coding sequence, and achieves the beam splitting performance with a compact size.

articleTitle: Design Challenges In Continuous Mode Power Amplifiers
abstract: This paper analyzes the appropriate design space for continuous mode power amplifiers that results into foster loads realizable with passive matching networks. An insight is presented to engineer the second harmonic loads to provide clockwise trajectory on Smith chart. This enables designers to choose the solutions which are feasible in terms of designing matching network. The scheme presented is validated with two waveform engineering based design examples using Continuous Class B/J and Continuous Class F modes of operation. A 15 W GaN HEMT transistors from Wolfspeed are used to design these power amplifiers to obtain high efficiency over a wide bandwidth.

articleTitle: A Compact On-chip CBCMLR-BPF Using Electromagnetic Parameters Extraction Method
abstract: In this paper, an on chip band-pass filter (BPF) is designed and fabricated in a 0.5 μm InP DHBT technology for terahertz applications. The designed resonator consists of two curved broadside-coupled meander-lines(CBCMLR) in opposite directions. A defected-ground structure (DGS) is used for a higher attenuation at the high-frequency band. Besides, an electromagnetic simulation method is proposed to establish a precise capacitor model at terahertz frequencies. By using the proposed structure and method, a compact BPF is designed. The simulated results show that the resonator can generate a resonance at 260 GHz with a 37-dB attenuation, and the BPF demonstrates a 2.3-dB insertion loss at 210 GHz and occupies 0.092 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> including the pads.

articleTitle: An Omnidirectionally Invisible Artificial Medium
abstract: An invisible solid medium in free space requires itself neither reflects nor refracts lights for all incident angles, which has not been found in nature. In this paper, we show that such a medium can be artificially achieved by constructing a mesoscopic building block with independently controllable electrical and magnetic resonances. By precise dispersion engineering, this building block could have both effective unity permittivity and permeability at a specific frequency. Composites consisting of either loosely or densely arranged such blocks can exhibit omnidirectional invisibility in free space, regardless of the shape. 3D sculpture technology was used to fabricate an electrically large aircraft sample for experimental verification. The measured results show that this artificial medium macroscopically exhibits an air-like electromagnetic response at around 5 GHz. The proposed medium can improve mechanical stability, electrical conduction, and heat dissipation of a system, without disturbing the electro-magnetic design.

articleTitle: Multiport Rectennas for Ambient RF Energy Harvesting
abstract: We describe techniques for using multiport antennas in rectennas suitable for ambient RF energy harvesting. Two antenna combining approaches, RF and dc combining, are briefly reviewed. Four impedance matching techniques, MCM, SOM, MLM, and SPM are also reviewed to show how impedance matching can compensate for the negative impact of mutual coupling in compact multiple antenna systems. Making use of these results three multiport rectenna design examples are also provided to show the benefit of using multiport rectenna to increase harvested RF energy. Using this multiport rectenna approach harvested ambient RF energy can exceed 10 μW in some environments, making them suitable for low power Internet of Things devices.

articleTitle: High-Gain High-Efficiency Integrated Array Antenna Based on MEMS Bulk Micromachining Technology for W-band Wireless Applications
abstract: In this invited paper, several W-band high-efficiency and high-gain integrated antenna arrays based on MEMS bulk micromachining technology are introduced. They are W-band high-efficiency high-gain wideband integrated array antenna and W-band high-efficiency high-gain two-dimensional low SLL integrated array antenna. Owing to the characteristics of high-gain and compact configuration, these types of antenna arrays can be excellent candidates for W-band wireless applications.

articleTitle: Frequency-Tripling OEO based on Frequency Multiplication in Saturated Low Phase Noise Amplifier
abstract: A Frequency-Tripling optoelectronic oscillator (FT-OEO) based on frequency multiplication in saturated low phase noise amplifier (LPNA) has been proposed and demonstrated. In the FT-OEO, the LPNA works in the saturated region and generates significant harmonic signals. The harmonic signals are coupled out from the loop and filtered as the output of the FT-OEO. A prototype of the FT-OEO, which oscillated at 2GHz, was constructed and the frequency-tripling signal at 6GHz was generated as the desired output. Comparison of the measured phase noise power spectrum density (PSD) of the fundamental signal with the frequency-tripling signal indicated that the additive phase noise of the amplifier is insignificant. Utilizing the saturated LPNA driven by the in-loop high-power oscillating signal, this FT-OEO provides a simple and cost-efficient scheme for frequency tripling.

articleTitle: High Performance 5G Antenna Radome Based on Absorptive Meta-surface
abstract: In this paper, a high-performance 5G radome based on absorptive meta-surface is proposed, where an unit cell structure consists of a dielectric layer which is sandwiched between a top lossy layer and a bottom metallic layer. The thickness of radome is designed only 0.037λ, where the simulation results show that the proposed radome is totally transparent to the working band from 3.2 GHz to 3.8 GHz, with an insertion loss less than 0.2dB. Moreover, the spurious signals from 6.5GHz to 7.5GHz could be highly absorbed, with the absorption efficiency more than 90%. The radome is independent to the electromagnetic(EM) waves in both TE and TM modes. The working principle of this radome is also explained reasonably in the perspective of the equivalent circuit model. These results are quite helpful in designing the miniaturized antenna device for 5G communications, radar and military communications.

articleTitle: Real-Time User Localisation in Beam Steered NIR Optical Wireless Communications
abstract: Near infrared (NIR) optical wireless communication provides a promising solution for point-to-point indoor high speed wireless data link. To cover a large area and several multiple users, wavelength-encoded laser beam steering has been demonstrated in previous research work. One remaining challenge in beam steered optical wireless system is real-time user localization. In this paper, ultrafast complete user localization at update rate of 10 MHz based on instantaneous optical wavelength detection and chirped pulse correlation has been demonstrated. Both angular position and absolute distance of each user have been accurately detected.

articleTitle: Full 2-Port Vector Network Analyzer using Nonlinear Calibration of Six-Port Reflectometer
abstract: This paper represents implementation of a low cost full 2-port vector network analyzer based on six port reflectometer (SPR). It consists two SPRs of different topologies designed at 2 GHz and a power splitter. A full two-port nonlinear calibration method has been followed to determine all the calibration coefficients. After determining the calibration coefficients, the nonlinear equations are solved using Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm to obtain magnitude and phase of S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>, S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</sub>, S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> & S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">22</sub> for various arbitrary loads. The results obtained through this system are comparable with that of a commercial VNA.

articleTitle: The Periodic Leaky-wave Antenna by Orthogonally Bending Microstrip Transmission Line with Open Stopband Elimination
abstract: The periodic leaky wave antenna (PLWA) by orthogonally bending microstrip transmission line is presented in this paper. The proposed antenna consists of periodically orthogonally bending microstrip transmission line. The calculation formula of the propagation wavenumber of this antenna is given, and the calculated results and measured results are matched. A simple technique to eliminate the open stopband (OSB) is presented. The prototype antenna was simulated, fabricated and measured, The measurement results show that the main beam scans continuously and from -55° to 63° in y-z plane when the operating frequency increasing from 3.7 GHz to 6.8 GHz. The structure of this PLWA is simple and easy to fabricate.

articleTitle: Design of a Ka-Band LFMCW Tracking Radar System with Background Learning
abstract: In this paper, a linear frequency modulated continuous wave (LFMCW) radar system was designed and established for detecting the distance and velocity of people and vehicles. The radar operates at 35 GHz with the maximum sweep frequency band of 2 GHz and uses triangular wave modulation. Background learning method is introduced to improve the system performance. Learning and recording the stationary background results after Moving Target Indication (MTI) filter is used as the threshold value for detecting moving targets. The designed radar system measured the distance and velocity of walking people and the speed error is less than 0.5 m/s.

articleTitle: Single Layer Optically Transparent Reflectarray Based on Indium Tin Oxide
abstract: Indium tin oxide (ITO) material is a practicable alternative to metal utilized in transparent antennas. However, the conductor loss of ITO material is the major obstacle to antenna design. In this work, a transparent ITO reflectarray based on glass substrate with ITO film operating at 28GHz is proposed. A single layer sub-wavelength element with 0.31 wavelength spacing is proposed in this reflectarray design. The peak loss of the proposed element is lower than 4dB while achieving a phase variation of 288° at 28GHz. A 30×30 elements reflectarray with a focus to diameter ratio (f/D) of 1 is designed and simulated for demonstration. It achieves more than 84% optical transparency and 75% radiation efficiency at the center frequency.

articleTitle: A W-Band Fully-Integrated Rectifier for Wireless Power Transfer in 0.1-μm GaAs Technology
abstract: This paper presents an on-chip fully integrated rectifier for wireless power transfer at W-band in 0.1-μm GaAs technology. The rectifier consists of an input matching network, a rectifying component and an output DC-pass filter. The rectifier achieves a measured maximum power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 13.8% at 99 GHz, with the PCE of more than 10% from 97.5 GHz to 100 GHz. The rectifier maintains a high PCE over a wide range of load resistances and has an input power range of up to 22 dBm. The entire chip occupies only 0.35 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> including pads.

articleTitle: A Millimeter-Wave On-Chip Bandpass Filter with All-Pole Characteristics
abstract: This paper presents a millimeter-wave on-chip bandpass filter (BPF) with all-pole characteristics. It is believed to be the first time that an all-pole frequency response has been successfully implemented by using a standard 0.13-μm Silicon-Germanium (SiGe) technology. To further demonstrate the feasibility of using this approach in practice, the designed resonator is fabricated. The measured results show that the BPF has an insertion loss of 2.2 dB at the center frequency of 31 GHz. The return loss is better than 10 dB from 26.5 GHz to 37.5 GHz. In addition, the out-of-band suppression of this filter is superior, which is better than 20 dB beyond 50.6 GHz. The chip size, excluding the pads, is only 0.091 × 0.268 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of 28GHz Phased Array Antenna System
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of a 28 GHz phased array antenna system which contains eight channels. Each channel contains a pair of 5-bit phase shifters and a pair of 5-bit digital step attenuators, which can be applied to separately tune the phase and amplitude of its either transmitting or receiving mode, and an eight-patch sub-array is connected to each channel. Therefore, the designed phased array system has altogether 64 patch elements and can perform one-dimensional beam scanning over an angle range of ±30°.

articleTitle: Evaluation on Probe-positioning Errors in Near-field Holographic Phase-less Measurement
abstract: The influence of the probe-positioning errors on planar near-field holographic phase-less measurement is displayed in this paper. Compared with the traditional near-field measurement, the near-field phase-less measurement diminishes the requirement of the stable and accurate phase. However, probe-positioning errors in phase-less near field measurement will still make the far field calculation results inaccuracy.
