A resistive square patch and resistive circular patch designed respectively at 16 GHz and 22 GHz are presented. Both designs show amplitude and phase variations for different resistivity values and element dimensions. These resistive elements can be printed on a substrate along with conventional metallic reflectarray elements resulting in a simplified reflectarray design without adding much fabrication complexity.

articleTitle: Automotive Radar Technology & Test Solution for Autonomus Driving
abstract: The automotive industry has repeatedly reinvented itself in recent decades. Networking and digitization are the meg-atrends and drivers of new business models. articleTitle: Improved Decoding Method for LDPC-COFDM System
abstract: In this paper, performance of LDPC-coded OFDM system at the presence of DF and NBI has been studied. As DF and NBI will always lead to burst errors at the receiver’s end, these un-decodable frames can make the BER performance suffering significantly degradation. In order to eliminate this problem, an improved decoding method for LDPC codes in LDPC-COFDM system is presented in this study. Firstly, a novel burst error identification scheme based on syndrome is produced. Secondly, a LLR-ZF method that can improve the decoding performance is proposed. Finally, simulations to testify the effectiveness of the proposed strategy are carried out.

articleTitle: An X-band space-borne low-profile lightweight patch antenna array using integrated design
abstract: An X-band patch antenna array with integrated design for satellite usage is described in this paper. By adopting the patch element and integrated design of the ground plane, the height and weight of the antenna array are greatly reduced. Using a solder-less connection between the radiating patch and the inner conductor, the proposed antenna array achieves the high-integration design. At the same time, the ground plane uses light metal material magnesium-lithium alloys that can further reduce the weight of the antenna. Compared with the same element number of the cross-dipole array, the height of the patch antenna array in this paper reduces by 70% and the weight reduces by 64.5%.

articleTitle: The Concurrent Inverse Class-F Mode for Concurrent Dual-Band RF Power Amplifiers
abstract: Based on current waveform shaping, a novel concurrent inverse Class-F (Class-F<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>) mode is presented for the concurrent dual-band power amplifier (PA). According to the analysis of proposed concurrent modes, the optimal load impedances are given for output matching circuit design at fundamental, harmonic and intermodulation (IM) frequency. The process of engineering current and voltage adopts the strong nonlinear model of PA and reveals that concurrent Class-F<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> mode may have better linearity performance because of class-A bias point. The theoretical results show that the proposed mode show more than 3.8 dB output power promotion compared with concurrent Class-B mode, which are driven by two CW signals with same amplitudes, which provides an opportunity and potential to design concurrent power amplifier.

articleTitle: Switched Type Phase Shifters using Controllable DGS in CMOS Technology for 79 GHz Automotive Phased Array Radar
abstract: This paper proposes a novel phase shifter by digitally control the path of the ground return current of defected ground structure (DGS) using NMOS switch. By switching on or off the ground return current to a shorter path or a longer path, the equivalent series inductance associated with the DGS cell can be tuned. Wide phase shift range and fine phase resolution can be achieved by cascading DGS cells longitudinally and transversally. Two phase shifters designed in 65nm CMOS technology with a core size of 0.112 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and 0.135 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> are presented for 79GHz automotive phased array radar. The phase shifting range and resolution for phase shifter I and II are 108°/2° and 155°/5° with a RMS phase error and gain error of 0.53°/1.01 dB and 1.25°/1.26 dB respectively.
